certainty_reasoning: Wikipedia carries the same, naming her and not the first wife.
date_label: C. 1920; still married at his death, 26 April 1957
summary: Fothergill married Kate Headley Kirby about 1920 and two years later took on the Spread Eagle at Thame. She ran it with him and he credited her in print; the inn made his name, and its collapse ended it. They were still married when he died in 1957.

sources.quote: two years after he had apparently resolved previous emotional ambivalences by marrying Kate Headley Kirby. In many respects, Kate was his salvation
sources.context: Sox on Fothergill's turn to innkeeping at forty-six. The index entry reads 'Kirby, Kate Headley (see Fothergill), 159, 162'.
sources.supports: The second marriage, the wife's name, and its dating relative to the Spread Eagle.
sources.provenance: David Sox, Bachelors of Art (1991), text layer

order_hint.why: Sox dates the marriage only as two years before Fothergill took up innkeeping at forty-six, which computes to about 1920 on his 1876 birth. No wedding date is stated anywhere read.

sources.quote: Under Fothergill's and his wife Kate's management, the Spread Eagle became a destination restaurant.
sources.context: Wikipedia, 'John Fothergill (innkeeper)'. The article separately records that Fothergill, in his 1931 An Innkeeper's Diary, credited his wife Kate with making the trifle on a regular basis - i.e. His own published testimony to the marriage.
sources.supports: Independent naming of Kate as Fothergill's wife and co-manager.
